objective: Replace honest active-branch width failure by a universally sufficient finite polynomial degree, while retaining the existing genuinely clipped branch and original negative-exponential target.
proposed_signatures_not_yet_sealed_or_co: For T,b:Nat, d=2*T^2+b+1, degree=2*d-1 and q:Rat with |q|<=T: radius(q,degree)<=1/2^(b+1).
For positive rational epsilon, T=tailCutoff(epsilon), degree=4*T^2+2*T+1, and q<=0: checked(q,epsilon,T,degree) returns some(bounds(q,T,degree)).
proposed_derivation: d>=1 and 2*T^2<=d. The last d factors of (2d)! give (2d)!>=d^d, with all inequalities to be proved in Lean.
Then |q|^(2d)/(2d)! <= (T^2/d)^d <= (1/2)^d <= 2^-(b+1). No floating e or free factorial estimate is used.
The active interval width is twice its remainder. Set b=T=the existing checked logarithmic cutoff; width<=2^-T<=epsilon.
The clipped branch already has width<=epsilon. Outside it, |q|<T is already proved, so Taylor need not take powers of arbitrarily large L-scaled q.
remaining_global_reserve_design: Radius has epsilon/4 certified. The four remaining contributions may provisionally reserve 3*epsilon/16 each, summing with radius to epsilon. This is accounting design only; no contribution is assumed closed or silently zero.

Any new rank/resource route needs its own sealed original-state approximation proof and stored producer. Do not substitute it silently for existing MPS-01/exact-real supplier.
